result:
I found and fixed the bug. `npm test` passes (10 of 10), and the 4 new tests fail if I put back the old source code, so they catch this bug.

**Root cause:** In `src/payments/gateway/payload.js`, the charge code lowercased the currency for the gateway (`"JPY"` became `"jpy"`). It then used that lowercase code to look up how many decimal places the currency has. The currency table in `src/lib/currency/registry.js` uses upper-case codes, so the lookup found nothing and fell back to the default of 2 decimals. A ¥1,500 invoice was therefore sent to the gateway as `1500 × 100 = 150000`, and since yen and won have no decimals, the gateway charged ¥150,000. US and EU customers weren't affected because their currencies use 2 decimals anyway, so the fallback happened to be right. The PDF was correct because the invoice code uses the upper-case code.

**Fix:**
- **`src/payments/gateway/payload.js`:** the amount is now calculated from the invoice's own upper-case currency code. The lowercase code is only used for the `currency` field sent to the gateway.
- **`src/lib/currency/registry.js`:** currency lookups now ignore upper/lower case. Refunds, payouts, coupons, late fees and proration use the same conversion, so a lowercase code from any of them would have had the same 100× error with no warning.

**Regression tests (`test/charge.test.js`):**
- A JPY invoice of 1500 is charged as 1500, with the gateway currency still `jpy`.
- A KRW invoice of 25000 is charged as 25000.
- A KWD invoice of 12.345 is charged as 12345 (3 decimals), which was also wrong before.
- The amount conversion gives the same result for `"jpy"` and `"JPY"`.

Customers in Japan, Korea and any other zero-decimal currency (VND and CLP are also set up) were overcharged 100×. Any KWD/BHD charges would have been undercharged by a factor of 10. Those charges will probably need to be found and refunded or corrected. The audit log's `invoice.charged` events record the wrong amount that was sent.

I haven't committed anything.
